## Merge vs Rebase

**Merge**: joins two branches by creating new "merge commit". History shows exactly what happened — parallel work, then join point.

**Rebase**: replays your commits on top of target branch. History looks linear, as if you branched from current tip.

---

### Merge
```
      A---B---C  feature
     /         \
D---E---F---G---H  main (merge commit H)
```
- Preserves real history
- Non-destructive (no commit SHA change)
- Adds merge commit noise on busy repos

### Rebase
```
              A'--B'--C'  feature (replayed)
             /
D---E---F---G  main
```
- Clean linear history
- Rewrites SHAs — **never rebase shared/public branches**
- Conflicts resolved commit-by-commit (more granular, also more annoying)

---

### When to use

| Situation | Use |
|-----------|-----|
| Feature branch → main (team repo) | **Merge** (preserves context, safe) |
| Updating local feature branch with main changes | **Rebase** (cleaner, not yet pushed) |
| Already pushed branch others depend on | **Merge** (rebase rewrites = force push = pain) |
| Personal/solo branch, want clean log | **Rebase** |
| Bisecting bugs, audit trail matters | **Merge** (real timestamps/parents) |

---

### Core rule

> Never rebase commits that exist outside your local repo.

Once SHA changes, anyone else with old SHA has diverged history. Force push required. Teammates cursed.

**Short answer**: rebase for clean local history before PR, merge for integrating into shared branches.
